title: fix(types): run the reader census through PCRE and pin an engine self-test
body:
Fixes #8361

Triage ruled **Option A**: switch the anchors to PCRE **and** add an engine self-test that names the engine when PCRE is missing. Triage's own point about the card's unverified "PCRE is compiled into both Apple Git and the CI git" assertion is that **the self-test is that assertion's verifier** — so the second half of A, not the flag swap, is the deliverable.

## The defect

`packages/types/src/__tests__/handler-keys-string-any-mirrors-7344.test.ts` built its `AppComponentSchema.actions[]` reader census with `git grep -E` and `\b` word-boundary anchors. **POSIX ERE has no `\b`** — nor `\s`, which two of the anchors also use. GNU regex adds both as extensions; the BSD regex library Apple Git links against does not. On a stock macOS host every anchor was therefore dead, the census read a tree with zero readers, and all five assertions failed reporting *"the anchor is dead"* — sending the reader after a tree change that had not happened. CI, on Linux, was green on the same bytes.

The liveness guard is what caught it at all, and is **untouched**: without it the file would have gone GREEN on macOS with a census of zero readers. What it could not do is separate *"the anchor is dead because the tree changed"* from *"...because this host's regex engine has no `\b`"`. Making that failure self-describing is what this PR adds.

## What changed (one test file + a changeset)

- One `GREP_ENGINE_FLAG = '-P'` replaces the five `-E` call sites; the two inline import anchors are named so the whole anchor set is visible to the pin below.
- **An engine self-test**, placed before the census, probing a synthetic three-line corpus in a temp dir *outside* the repo (so it measures the engine, not this tree, and cannot be answered by the file it lives in). It fails **naming the git it ran on** when that git has no PCRE, when `\b` is not a boundary, and when `\b` is read as the literal letter `b`. Its two negatives carry a `-F` control proving all three lines reached the scanner — the same control the census demands of itself.
- **A pin** that every anchor carrying `\b`/`\s` must run through `-P`, so the flag cannot be reverted one anchor at a time.
- `gitGrepFiles` now treats **only exit 1** ("no matches") as a reading. Every other status is raised as *the tool failing*, quoting git's status and stderr, instead of being laundered into an empty census — that laundering is what let an engine difference wear a tree change's clothes.

## Verification

⚠️ **I am on Linux (git 2.43.0), where GNU `-E` honours `\b`, so I cannot reproduce the failure directly.** It is proved the way the card proved the defect — by pairing engine flags on one tree — plus two ablations.

**1. The switch is census-neutral on the CI engine.** Same tree, same patterns, one flag changed; file sets compared, not just counts:

| anchor | `-E` | `-P` | diff |
|---|---|---|---|
| `\.actions\b` | 112 | 112 | 0 lines |
| `\bapp[…]\??\.actions\b` (`-i`) | 3 | 3 | 0 lines |
| `^\s*import[^;]*\bAppAction\b` | 2 | 2 | 0 lines |
| `^\s*import[^;]*\bAppComponentSchema\b` | 13 | 13 | 0 lines |
| `\bAppAction\b` | 8 | 8 | 0 lines |

All exit 0. ⇒ PCRE **is** compiled into this container's git, and the switch changes no verdict on a GNU host.

**2. The self-test genuinely fails, and names the engine.** A PATH shim standing in for a git built without `USE_LIBPCRE` (dies 128 on `-P`, passes everything else through):

```
AssertionError: `git grep -P` could not run. This is the ENGINE, not the tree:
git version 2.43.0 said "fatal: cannot use Perl-compatible regexes when not
compiled with USE_LIBPCRE". A git built without PCRE (`USE_LIBPCRE`) dies here;
the census anchors need `\b`, which POSIX ERE does not have, so `-E` is not a
fallback — rebuild or install a git with PCRE: expected 128 to be +0
```

and the census, instead of reporting an empty tree:

```
Error: `git grep -l -P \.actions\b` exited 128 — the TOOL failed, this is NOT a
reading of an empty tree. Engine: git version 2.43.0, regex flag `-P`. git said:
fatal: cannot use Perl-compatible regexes when not compiled with USE_LIBPCRE
```

**3. The defect reproduced in emulation, original vs fixed, same host.** A second shim emulates Apple Git on BSD regex: an `-E` pattern containing `\b`/`\s` matches nothing (exit 1), `-P` passes through. It reproduces the card's reading shape — `-E '\.actions\b'` → 0 files, `-P` → 112; `-E` on the import anchor → 0, `-P` → 13 — while `-E` *without* `\b` still returns 19 files, so the shim breaks only the POSIX-undefined escapes.

| file at | git | result |
|---|---|---|
| `1cca4415e` (pre-fix) | BSD-regex shim | **5 failed** / 57, messages *"the anchor is dead"*, *"contributed no file to the population"*, *"the import anchor found nothing at all"* — the card's five, verbatim |
| `a8da9b790` (this PR) | **same** shim | **61 passed** |

The mutation was proven on disk before the run (`'-E'` occurrences 0 → 5, `GREP_ENGINE_FLAG` 13 → 0, blob `e69d766f8`), and the restore proven by state afterwards (blob back to `cbeb46e31`, `git diff HEAD` empty), not by any exit code.

**4. Gates**, at `a8da9b790`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` → **147 files, 2811 tests, all passed** (was 57 tests in this file, now 61)
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run type-check` → exit 0; `tsc --listFiles` confirms this file is **in** the program (count 1, not excluded)
- `pnpm exec turbo run lint` — the **whole repo**, not a narrowed subset: **47/47 tasks successful**, 0 errors
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` → all exit 0
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` → **NOT GOVERNED** (2 paths, no surface matched)

An empty-frontmatter changeset declares the change as releasing nothing (`skip-changeset` is a phantom label in this repo and was not applied).

⚠️ `Bundle Analysis` is red on `main` and on every PR that triggers it — objectui#8542, not this change.

## Scope

Triage re-measured that exactly **1** test file pairs a `git grep` shell-out with `-E` + `\b` (this one) and **0** `scripts/check-*.mjs` gates do; that still holds at `1cca4415e`. #8404's three `scripts/__tests__` host-dependencies are a different mechanism and are not widened into here.

## What this PR does not verify

The card's assertion that PCRE is compiled into the **CI runner's** git is verified for this container's git 2.43.0 only. That is the assertion the self-test now exists to answer: if CI's git lacks PCRE, this PR's own check run says so and names the engine.
